evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:32-38 — PRICE_MAP_CACHE is a process-global HashMap<String, CacheEntry> (OnceLock<Arc<RwLock<..>>>) with NO size cap and NO eviction policy other than TTL expiry. The map key embeds raw, attacker-controlled request parameters: cache_key = format!("{}:{}:{}:{}", mode, time_window_str, query.property_type.unwrap_or(""), query.city.unwrap_or("")) at :125-131, where query.city and query.property_type are free-form strings taken straight off the public, UNAUTHENTICATED GET /api/v1/price-map handler (get_price_map(State, Query<PriceMapQuery>) at :97-100 — no RequestPrincipal / no auth extractor).

Memory-exhaustion DoS: the only reclamation is cache.retain(|_, v| Instant::now() < v.expires_at) at :229 run on the write path, and CACHE_TTL = Duration::from_secs(3600) (:41). Entries live a full hour before they become eligible for retain to drop them; an attacker issuing GET /api/v1/price-map?city=<unique-random-string> on a loop inserts a brand-new, never-expiring-within-the-window entry on every distinct city value (:227-234 unconditionally cache.insert(cache_key, ...)). Each city only has to differ by one byte; it does not need to match any real listing (the query runs city ILIKE $3 and caches even an empty district vector). Millions of distinct keys accumulate within the 1h TTL → unbounded heap growth → OOM on a public endpoint.

Self-inconsistency: state.rs:910-915 (INQUIRY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_IPS = 100_000, built with with_default_bounded) explicitly bounds memory against an attacker rotating source IPs; the price_map cache, keyed on an equally attacker-influenced string space, has no equivalent bound. Fix (backend-only, cloud-landable): cap the map (bounded LRU / size-limited insert that evicts oldest once a MAX_ENTRIES ceiling is hit, mirroring the inquiry limiter), and/or normalise+reject out-of-allowlist city/property_type before they reach the key, and/or key the cache on a hash of validated inputs only.

price_map.rs:158-206 and listings.rs:700-706 both build query text with format!(...) and execute via sqlx::query(sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(sql)) / sqlx::query_as::<_, _>(sqlx::AssertSqlSafe(sql)). AssertSqlSafe is a deliberate opt-out of sqlx's compile-time/runtime SQL-safety checking — it tells sqlx 'trust me, this string is safe', disabling the one framework guard against interpolated-value injection.

Both sites are SAFE AS WRITTEN TODAY: listings.rs interpolates only the RICH_LISTING_SELECT const (:703) and binds all user values; price_map.rs interpolates only interval, which at :109-123 is the result of a closed match time_window_str.as_str() returning fixed literals ('1 month'/'3 months'/'12 months'/'5 years') and 400-ing on anything else. This is a latent-footgun / refactor-smell finding, not a live injection.

Risk: safety now rests on reviewer vigilance that every current and future format! argument stays a constant or an allowlisted literal. A later edit interpolating a less-controlled value (sort column, city, dynamic WHERE fragment) would silently introduce SQL injection with no macro error. Fix: add an explicit // SAFETY: ... comment at each AssertSqlSafe call, or migrate dynamic portions to sqlx::QueryBuilder.
